---
title: "Do CV strategies differ in model-to-model *consistency*?"
subtitle: "Permutation test of replicate dispersion across holdout strategies"
author: "Reed Benkendorf"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    code-fold: true
    df-print: paged
params:
  metric: "pr_auc"        # pr_auc | roc_auc | cox_slope | cox_intercept | nAP
  resolution: "3arc"      # 3arc (~90 m) | 1arc (~30 m) | 1-3arc
  source: "own"           # own  = model's own test holdout (all_fit_metrics.csv)
                          # gt   = 2026 field ground truth, interpolation domain (all_fit_2026gt.csv)
  min_reps: 2             # min seeds per (resolution x ratio x distOrder) cell to score its spread
  dispersion: "sd"        # sd | mad   (per-cell spread statistic)
  B: 9999                 # permutation resamples
  seed: 1
---

> **Question.** Eyeballing the refinement grids, the *random* (classic) holdout looks like its
> per-model precision scatters more widely than the spatial strategies — i.e. random is the
> least *consistent* replicate-to-replicate. Is that spread genuinely larger, or an artifact of
> random simply having more fits spread across the whole PA-ratio sweep?
>
> **Design.** "Consistency" is spread **at matched conditions**. The ratio sweep and resolution
> move the metric around for real reasons, so we never compare raw pooled spread. Instead:
>
> 1. A **cell** = one `(tree, resolution, PAratio, distOrder)` combination. Within a cell the only
>    thing that varies is the **seed** (the replicate).
> 2. Each cell with `>= min_reps` seeds yields one **dispersion** value (SD or MAD across seeds).
> 3. Those cell-level dispersions, tagged by CV strategy, are the data. A **permutation test**
>    shuffles the strategy labels across cells to ask whether random's typical within-cell spread
>    is larger than chance.
>
> This is re-runnable: as LMPO / spatial-mapping / finer-resolution fits land, rerun and the
> spatial strategies gain scoreable cells. The replication table below shows how thin each
> strategy currently is.

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
set.seed(params$seed)

PROJ <- "/home/sagesteppe/Documents/Ecoloradense"   # adjust per machine
cv_lab <- c(Results_random_iter1a_high_pa        = "classic/random",
            Results_spatialknn_iter1a_high_pa     = "spatial kNN",
            Results_spatialmapping_iter1a_high_pa = "spatial mapping",
            Results_LMPO_iter1a_high_pa           = "LMPO")
RES <- params$resolution
```

## Build the per-fit table

One row per fitted model, carrying the chosen `metric`. `own` reads the model's own
test-split metrics; `gt` reads the 2026 field ground truth and pools the two interpolation
distance bins (`<=270m`, `>270m`) by point count. nAP = (PR-AUC − prevalence)/(1 − prevalence),
with the own-split prevalence taken from the PA ratio and the GT prevalence from the field subset.

```{r build}
pa_prev <- function(x) {                         # "1:1.023" -> prevalence 1/(1+1.023)
  r <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("^1:", "", x))); ifelse(is.na(r), NA, 1 / (1 + r))
}

per_fit <- if (params$source == "own") {
  read.csv(file.path(PROJ, "results_summary/all_fit_metrics.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    filter(tree %in% names(cv_lab), resolution == RES) |>
    mutate(prevalence = pa_prev(PAratio),
           nAP = (pr_auc - prevalence) / (1 - prevalence)) |>
    select(fname, tree, resolution, PAratio, distOrder, seed,
           pr_auc, roc_auc, cox_slope, cox_intercept, nAP)
} else {
  read.csv(file.path(PROJ, "results_summary/all_fit_2026gt.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    filter(tree %in% names(cv_lab), resolution == RES, grepl("^Interp", domain)) |>
    group_by(fname, tree, resolution, PAratio, distOrder, seed) |>   # pool the 2 interp bins
    summarise(pr_auc        = weighted.mean(pr_auc, n),
              roc_auc       = weighted.mean(roc_auc, n),
              cox_slope     = weighted.mean(cox_slope, n),
              cox_intercept = weighted.mean(cox_intercept, n),
              prevalence    = weighted.mean(prevalence, n), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(nAP = (pr_auc - prevalence) / (1 - prevalence))
}

stopifnot(params$metric %in% names(per_fit))
per_fit$value <- per_fit[[params$metric]]
per_fit$cv    <- factor(cv_lab[per_fit$tree], levels = cv_lab)
per_fit       <- per_fit[!is.na(per_fit$value), ]
cat(sprintf("source=%s  metric=%s  resolution=%s  -> %d fits\n",
            params$source, params$metric, RES, nrow(per_fit)))
```

## How much replication exists? (read this first)

The permutation test can only use cells with `>= min_reps` seeds. If a strategy has almost no
such cells, it simply can't be compared yet — that is the week-of-compute reality, not a result.

```{r replication}
cells <- per_fit |>
  group_by(cv, resolution, PAratio, distOrder) |>
  summarise(reps = n(), .groups = "drop")

avail <- cells |>
  group_by(cv) |>
  summarise(total_cells   = n(),
            scoreable      = sum(reps >= params$min_reps),
            max_reps       = max(reps),
            median_reps    = median(reps), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(avail, caption = sprintf("Cells per strategy at %s (scoreable = >= %d seeds)",
                                      RES, params$min_reps))

ggplot(cells, aes(PAratio, cv, fill = reps)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey90") +
  geom_text(aes(label = reps), size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eef3ff", high = "#2c5fa8", name = "seeds") +
  labs(title = "Replicate seeds per condition", x = "PA ratio", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
```

## Cell-level dispersion

```{r dispersion}
disp_fun <- if (params$dispersion == "mad") function(x) mad(x) else function(x) sd(x)

cell_disp <- per_fit |>
  group_by(cv, resolution, PAratio, distOrder) |>
  filter(n() >= params$min_reps) |>
  summarise(reps = n(), disp = disp_fun(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(is.finite(disp))

usable <- cell_disp |> group_by(cv) |>
  summarise(cells = n(), median_disp = round(median(disp), 4),
            mean_disp = round(mean(disp), 4), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(usable, caption = sprintf("Scoreable cells and typical within-cell %s of %s",
                                       toupper(params$dispersion), params$metric))

ggplot(cell_disp, aes(cv, disp)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey95") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, alpha = 0.5, aes(size = reps)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 3.5)) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Within-condition replicate %s of %s (%s)",
                       toupper(params$dispersion), params$metric, RES),
       subtitle = "each point = one (ratio x distOrder) cell; higher = less consistent",
       x = NULL, y = sprintf("%s(%s) across seeds", toupper(params$dispersion), params$metric)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Permutation test — omnibus

Null hypothesis: within-cell dispersion is exchangeable across CV strategies (labels carry no
information). Test statistic: the Kruskal–Wallis `H` on the cell-level dispersions (rank-based,
so it does not assume normal dispersions). We shuffle the strategy labels across cells `B` times
and compare.

```{r perm-omnibus}
grp_ok <- cell_disp |> count(cv) |> filter(n >= 2) |> pull(cv)
cd <- cell_disp |> filter(cv %in% grp_ok) |> mutate(cv = droplevels(cv))

if (nlevels(cd$cv) < 2 || nrow(cd) < 6) {
  cat("Not enough scoreable cells across >=2 strategies yet — rerun once the grid fills.\n")
} else {
  kw_H <- function(y, g) unname(kruskal.test(y, g)$statistic)
  obs  <- kw_H(cd$disp, cd$cv)
  perm <- replicate(params$B, kw_H(cd$disp, sample(cd$cv)))
  p    <- (1 + sum(perm >= obs)) / (params$B + 1)
  cat(sprintf("Omnibus KW H = %.2f over %d strategies, %d cells\n",
              obs, nlevels(cd$cv), nrow(cd)))
  cat(sprintf("Permutation p = %.4g  (parametric KW p = %.4g)\n",
              p, kruskal.test(cd$disp, cd$cv)$p.value))
  hist(perm, breaks = 40, col = "grey85", border = "white",
       main = "Permutation null for KW H", xlab = "H under shuffled labels")
  abline(v = obs, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2);
}
```

## Permutation test — is *random* the least consistent?

Targeted one-sided contrast: observed statistic = median within-cell dispersion of **random**
minus median of **all other** strategies pooled. Positive = random more variable. The null
shuffles the random / not-random label across cells.

```{r perm-random}
if (!"classic/random" %in% levels(droplevels(cell_disp$cv)) ||
    sum(cell_disp$cv == "classic/random") < 2 ||
    sum(cell_disp$cv != "classic/random") < 2) {
  cat("Need >=2 scoreable cells for random and >=2 for the rest — not yet.\n")
} else {
  is_rand <- cell_disp$cv == "classic/random"
  stat <- function(flag) median(cell_disp$disp[flag]) - median(cell_disp$disp[!flag])
  obs  <- stat(is_rand)
  perm <- replicate(params$B, stat(sample(is_rand)))
  p_gt <- (1 + sum(perm >= obs)) / (params$B + 1)   # random MORE variable
  cat(sprintf("median disp: random = %.4f, rest = %.4f, difference = %+.4f\n",
              median(cell_disp$disp[is_rand]), median(cell_disp$disp[!is_rand]), obs))
  cat(sprintf("one-sided permutation p (random MORE variable) = %.4g\n", p_gt))

  # pairwise random vs each other strategy
  cat("\nPairwise (random vs each), one-sided permutation p that random is more variable:\n")
  for (g in setdiff(levels(droplevels(cell_disp$cv)), "classic/random")) {
    sub <- cell_disp |> filter(cv %in% c("classic/random", g))
    if (sum(sub$cv == g) < 2) { cat(sprintf("  %-16s (too few cells)\n", g)); next }
    fr  <- sub$cv == "classic/random"
    st  <- function(f) median(sub$disp[f]) - median(sub$disp[!f])
    o   <- st(fr); pp <- (1 + sum(replicate(params$B, st(sample(fr))) >= o)) / (params$B + 1)
    cat(sprintf("  %-16s diff=%+.4f  p=%.4g  (n_random=%d, n_%s=%d)\n",
                g, o, pp, sum(fr), g, sum(!fr)))
  }
}
```

## Secondary: overall pooled spread (descriptive only)

This is what the eye catches in the grids — total spread of each strategy's models, **including**
the ratio sweep. Fligner–Killeen is a robust test of equal variance, but across the *raw* values
it conflates genuine inconsistency with the sweep, so treat it as a description, not the test.

```{r overall}
per_fit |> group_by(cv) |>
  summarise(n = n(), sd = round(sd(value), 4), iqr = round(IQR(value), 4),
            mad = round(mad(value), 4), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Pooled spread of %s (NOT condition-matched)", params$metric))

if (nlevels(droplevels(per_fit$cv)) >= 2)
  print(fligner.test(value ~ droplevels(cv), data = per_fit))
```

## Caveats

- **Replication gates everything.** Until a strategy has several `>= min_reps` cells, it cannot
  enter the test. Rerun as fits land; the availability table tracks progress.
- **Own vs GT.** `source: own` tests consistency of each model's self-assessment; `source: gt`
  tests consistency of true field (interpolation) performance. They can disagree — the own-holdout
  confound ([[cv-comparison-own-holdout-confound]]) means a strategy can be self-consistent yet
  inconsistent against the field, or vice versa.
- **Cells are the unit.** Permuting labels across cells (not individual fits) respects that seeds
  within a cell are not independent draws.
- **Dispersion choice.** `sd` is the natural "precision" spread; `mad` is robust to a single wild
  replicate. If they disagree, a few outlier fits are driving `sd` — worth reporting both.
- **Metric scale.** `cox_slope`/`cox_intercept` live on a different scale than `pr_auc`; compare
  dispersion only within one metric, never across.
```
